quickVerdict: These solve different problems more than they compete: Help Scout is a shared inbox with AI layered on top, Chatbase is an AI chatbot with a light inbox layered on top. Pick Help Scout if your support is mostly email and human conversation and you want AI Answers as a source-fenced self-service add-on. Pick Chatbase if your support starts on a website and you want the AI to be the front line, with humans as the fallback. Most teams already know which of those two sentences describes them before they open this comparison — the harder decision is usually price, since Help Scout's per-user model and Chatbase's per-credit model scale very differently as you grow. Neither vendor's AI-resolution numbers should be taken at face value.
tldr: Help Scout is a fourteen-year-old shared inbox built around email and live chat, with AI Answers added afterward as a $0.75-per-resolution self-service layer. Chatbase is an AI-chatbot builder first, with a helpdesk layer bolted on at higher tiers.

Pricing shapes are very different: Help Scout charges per user ($25/$45/$75/mo) plus $0.75 per AI resolution; Chatbase charges per message-credit pool ($40/$150/$500/mo, or $32/$120/$400 annually) regardless of headcount.

Help Scout's AI is deliberately narrow — it answers only from your Docs knowledge base and specified sources, with no order lookups or actions in connected systems. Chatbase's Actions system goes further, with real Shopify order lookups and Stripe billing actions built in.

Help Scout wins decisively on inbox quality and team collaboration — internal notes, assignment, a real ticketing-free shared view — while Chatbase wins on integration breadth for a website-first bot (WhatsApp, voice, Zendesk/HubSpot/Salesforce hooks at higher tiers).

Neither AI holds up to close scrutiny: Help Scout's 73.19% resolution figure counts any session the customer didn't escalate as a win, and Chatbase users report it confidently generating wrong answers once a question falls outside trained content.

Pick Help Scout if your team is answering real human conversations and wants AI as a deflection layer on top. Pick Chatbase if you want an AI-first website bot and are comfortable with credit-based, harder-to-predict billing.

verdict: The honest way to frame this comparison is that Help Scout and Chatbase were built to solve different first problems, and the differences downstream all trace back to that. Help Scout spent fourteen years perfecting a shared inbox that never makes a customer see a ticket number, and AI Answers arrived afterward as a genuinely restrained, source-fenced self-service layer — it answers from your Docs and nothing else, escalates cleanly, and doesn't bill you when it does. That restraint is also its ceiling: it cannot look up an order or take an action anywhere, so if your support volume is transactional ecommerce questions, Help Scout's AI isn't doing the actual work regardless of how good your documentation is. Chatbase inverts the build order — the AI agent is the product, and it's meaningfully more capable in the ways that matter for a website-first support flow: a real Shopify Action for order questions, a Stripe Action for billing, and multi-step Actions that can escalate or execute rather than just answer. What it doesn't have is Help Scout's inbox discipline; the helpdesk layer that unlocks at Standard tier is there to catch what the AI can't handle, not to run a team's day-to-day human conversation flow. Price shakes out differently depending on your shape: a five-person Help Scout team on Standard is $125/month plus AI resolutions, while a Chatbase Standard plan is a flat $150/month (or $120 annually) regardless of headcount — cheaper for a bigger team, more expensive for a small one leaning on a handful of agents. Neither vendor's AI-resolution numbers survive scrutiny: Help Scout's 73.19% figure counts an abandoned chat as a win, and Chatbase users report confidently wrong answers once a question strays from trained content. My honest read: if your team is having real conversations and wants AI as a deflection layer underneath a great inbox, start with Help Scout. If your support starts on a website and you want an AI-first agent that can actually look things up, start with Chatbase — just model your real message volume against a premium model's credit burn before you commit to a tier.
